newsitem.title: UK: Liberty steps into UK pensions with Hermes link.
newsitem.headline: Liberty steps into UK pensions with Hermes link.

text.p: Financial services and property group Liberty International said on Thursday it had formed a strategic alliance with Hermes Investment Management as part of a move into the British pensions market.

The two are creating a new subsidiary called Hermes Liberty International Pensions (HLIP) which will offer "specialised investment services to the UK pensions industry, with Hermes acting as fund manager", they said in a joint statement.
Britain's BT Pension Scheme, which owns Hermes, said it would transfer 1.5 billion pounds ($2.3 billion) of its assets into new funds offered by the new company.
This was welcomed by Liberty's chairman Donald Gordon as giving the venture critical mass from the outset.

"Initially HLIP will offer a UK index tracking fund and an actively enhanced UK index fund...It is anticipated that HLIP will be operational by the second quarter of 1997 once regulatory approvals have been obtained," the groups said.

The products on offer would be particularly suitable for occupational pension schemes and represent specific areas of specialisation for Hermes, one of the UK's largest pension fund management groups, they added.

Liberty is also setting up a new specialist pensions company called Liberty International Pensions. The BT Pension Scheme will pay 5.0 million pounds for 10 percent of the equity while Liberty will retain the balance.
This will meet the needs of money purchase pension schemes and offer personal pensions to retail customers, Liberty said.
Liberty International Pensions will be launched later this year once it has received Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) authorisation, which is expected shortly.

The new company will target visitors to Liberty International's regional shopping centres, which are held through majority-owned subsidiary Capital Shopping Centres and have more than 150 million customer visits a year, Liberty said. ($ = 0.639 British Pounds)
